text:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT P1 - Streaming tail latency SLO breach on /v1/stream (us-west-2). p99 > 5s for the last 10m. Paging oncall Alex. See alert: https://ops.redwood/alerts/2201234567

Alex: on it. seeing p95 jump ~300ms -> ~1.8s, p99 ~6.4s. streaming stalls flagged (clients seeing chunk gaps). will triage.

Maya: joining. do we have a hot node or multi-tenant correlation? any new deploys?

Alex: no deploys in last 30m. initial query shows spike concentrated on GPU pool pool-gpu-shared-2.

Sam: +1 noisy-neighbor suspicion. recent batch job from tenant "KiteSearch" started a large checkpoint around 10:24 which hit NVMe. Could be blkio saturation.

Alex: grabbing diagnostics now.

Alex: kubectl exec into node diagnostics -> iostat / nvme stats. output snippet:
```
# iostat -x 1 3
Device: rrqm/s wrqm/s r/s w/s rsec/s wsec/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await r_await w_await svctm %util
nvme0n1 0.00 2.00 0.00 125.00 0 320000 5120 8.72 45.00 0.10 60.00 1.20 98.5
```
Shows very high %util on nvme0n1.

Maya: yep. also seeing node-level iowait spike in monitoring. top processes by blkio: PID 24831 (trainer-checkpoint) from tenant KiteSearch eating >90% write throughput.

Sam: confirm. nvidia-smi shows GPUs busy but kernel I/O wait is the factor for stalls. Streaming paths hit local KV cache which reads from NVMe; when NVMe is saturated, KV reads stall and streaming stalls.

Katie: customers reported: AcmeApp (critical), KiteSearch (internal heavy job), Pixly (degraded streaming). Need customer impact assessment for pager duty.

Alex: quick impact summary: AcmeApp ~40% of requests to /v1/stream in us-west-2 observed increased tail latency and some partial responses requiring client reconnect. Pixly ~15% error/retry rate increase. KiteSearch is the noisy neighbor (self-inflicted).

Maya: mitigation options: 1) throttle/limit blkio for offending cgroup, 2) evict/move KiteSearch job to dedicated reserved pool, 3) enable fallback to smaller model for affected tenants, 4) temporarily increase NVMe IO quota if available.

Sam: applying cgroup blkio throttle is lowest-risk and fastest. I can reduce write_bps_device on that pod's cgroup. command: 
```
# example (on node):
echo "8:0 10485760" > /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/containers/<container-id>/blkio.throttle.write_bps_device
```
I'll prepare a safe throttle value (~10MB/s) then ramp up if stable.

Alex: Maya, do we want to drain the node as well? draining will cause model reloading cost and might worsen p95 temporarily due to pod rescheduling.

Maya: prefer throttle first. if stalls persist after 2-3 minutes, plan evict+drain. notify customers proactively.

Sam: applying throttle now to container-id abc123 (KiteSearch checkpoint job).

Sam: applied throttle -> 10MB/s. monitoring...

Alex: graphs show immediate drop in node nvme util to ~55% and p99 down from 6.4s to ~2.2s within 30s. p95 back to ~420ms. Streaming chunk gap count falling. :thumbsup:

Katie: I'll draft customer message for AcmeApp & Pixly. short note + mitigation steps + ETA.

Maya: good. please include that we applied an I/O throttle to a colocated tenant and are monitoring effects. call out possible future action (eviction to dedicated pool).

Alex: Sam — can you open a migration job to move KiteSearch to dedicated-reserved-1? we should schedule after the immediate spike is stable to avoid making it worse.

Sam: creating migration ticket and will coordinate with infra to provision reserved slot. ETA ~20-30m.

Maya: also checking cgroup and kernel messages. dmesg shows blkio throttling events and some IO timeouts from NVMe controller earlier. copying snippet:
```
[2201234560.123] nvme nvme0: I/O 0x7f failed, status: 5
[2201234562.456] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 123456789
```
Not seeing disk failure but high queue depth.

Lee: jumping in — if we need immediate relief we can failover traffic for AcmeApp to us-west-1 by updating routing policy for that customer. would be a manual override but fastest for that customer.

Alex: good option if p99 doesn't settle below 1s. we have 1.5h runway before we start eviction.

Sam: migration ticket created: INFRA-4729. moving KiteSearch job to dedicated-reserved-1 after 15m cooldown.

Maya: confirm monitoring windows: will observe for 30m post-mitigation. set incident state -> monitoring.

incidents-bot: Incident 2201234567 state changed to MONITORING by Maya. SLA impact: degraded streaming for AcmeApp/Pixly for ~10-25m.

Katie: message to AcmeApp sent: "We observed elevated streaming latency due to high I/O contention from a colocated job. We have applied temporary I/O throttling and are monitoring. Expect reduced tail latency within minutes; we will follow up with root cause and remediation steps."

Alex: handoff — I need to go to another page. Lee, you take follow-up (migration verification + postmortem owner). I will update handoff channel.

Lee: taking it. I'll watch migration and confirm the dedicated-reserved slot is healthy. assigning postmortem INFRA-PM-2201.

Maya: follow-ups: - confirm kernel/I/O timeouts don't repeat after migration - add automated detection for long-running checkpoint writes that exceed blkio thresholds - consider per-tenant KV cache QoS to reduce local NVMe dependence for streaming paths.

Sam: I also recommend adding a preemptible background-checkpoint limiter in the runtime to pause heavy writes when node IO crosses 70% util. filing a runtime task.

Alex: thanks team. final notes: incident duration ~25m, primary cause = noisy neighbor performing heavy NVMe writes -> IO saturation -> KV cache reads blocked -> streaming tail latency + partial client disconnects. mitigation = cgroup blkio throttle -> p99 improved, then schedule migration to dedicated pool.

Lee: closing channel for now, will update when migration complete. :white_check_mark:
